suggestions: pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
convert an IN subquery to a semi-join
optimized_sql:
SELECT item.i_item_id,
       SUM(agg.ss_quantity_sum::numeric) / NULLIF(SUM(agg.ss_quantity_cnt), 0) AS agg1,
       SUM(agg.ss_list_price_sum::numeric) / NULLIF(SUM(agg.ss_list_price_cnt), 0) AS agg2,
       SUM(agg.ss_coupon_amt_sum::numeric) / NULLIF(SUM(agg.ss_coupon_amt_cnt), 0) AS agg3,
       SUM(agg.ss_sales_price_sum::numeric) / NULLIF(SUM(agg.ss_sales_price_cnt), 0) AS agg4
FROM (
    SELECT ss_item_sk,
           SUM(ss_quantity) AS ss_quantity_sum,
           COUNT(ss_quantity) AS ss_quantity_cnt,
           SUM(ss_list_price) AS ss_list_price_sum,
           COUNT(ss_list_price) AS ss_list_price_cnt,
           SUM(ss_coupon_amt) AS ss_coupon_amt_sum,
           COUNT(ss_coupon_amt) AS ss_coupon_amt_cnt,
           SUM(ss_sales_price) AS ss_sales_price_sum,
           COUNT(ss_sales_price) AS ss_sales_price_cnt
    FROM store_sales
    WHERE ss_sold_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_dim WHERE d_year = 2001)
      AND ss_cdemo_sk IN (SELECT cd_demo_sk FROM customer_demographics WHERE cd_gender = 'F' AND cd_marital_status = 'W' AND cd_education_status = 'College')
      AND ss_promo_sk IN (SELECT p_promo_sk FROM promotion WHERE p_channel_email = 'N' OR p_channel_event = 'N')
    GROUP BY ss_item_sk
) AS agg
JOIN item ON item.i_item_sk = agg.ss_item_sk
GROUP BY item.i_item_id
ORDER BY item.i_item_id
LIMIT 100

1. FILTERED-KEY SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk / date_dim.d_year — TRANSFORMATION: replace the inner join to date_dim with a semi-join on the set of d_date_sk where d_year=2001, so only that year’s store_sales rows survive before any aggregation.

2. FILTERED-KEY SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_cdemo_sk / customer_demographics.cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status — TRANSFORMATION: replace the inner join to customer_demographics with a semi-join on the set of cd_demo_sk where cd_gender='F' AND cd_marital_status='W' AND cd_education_status='College', shrinking the fact rows before the next join.

3. FILTERED-KEY SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_promo_sk / promotion.p_channel_email, p_channel_event — TRANSFORMATION: replace the inner join to promotion with a semi-join on the set of p_promo_sk where p_channel_email='N' OR p_channel_event='N', so only store_sales rows tied to qualifying promotions remain.

4. AGGREGATION PUSHDOWN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_item_sk / item.i_item_id — TRANSFORMATION: aggregate the filtered store_sales by ss_item_sk first, carrying SUM and COUNT for ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_coupon_amt, and ss_sales_price; then join that compact result to item on i_item_sk and compute the final AVG per i_item_id, avoiding the expensive fact-to-item join before grouping.

5. COVERING INDEX — TARGET: store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk, ss_cdemo_sk, ss_promo_sk, ss_item_sk — TRANSFORMATION: create/use an index on these columns INCLUDE (ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_coupon_amt, ss_sales_price) so the three semi-joins and the pre-aggregation can be done with index-only scans.
